Under the pipeline-capability rule this issue leaves that work to the open PRs. Taking it on here (B or C) would widen scope and overlap three open PRs.
Q2: I checked both defects in the checkout. `tests/test_workflow_log_analysis_purge_safety.py:49-51` builds `_recent_doc()` as today minus two days, and `tests/test_workflow_log_analysis_report_pr.py:33` hard-codes `REPORT = "analysis/workflow-optimization-2026-11-09.md"`, so the two paths are the same on 2026-11-11. In `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py`, line 4661 allows `elapsed_ms=-?\d+`, but lines 4662 and 4669 require `\d+`. The fixes are small, test-only and deterministic. #9246 targets `main` and #9271 targets `orchestrator/project-9116`, so neither is guaranteed to reach the branch this fix needs. If one of them lands first, these edits become a no-op or a trivial conflict, so going ahead (A) carries the least risk. B would leave half of the known CI failure unfixed, and C would rest on PRs that have not merged.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q2:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - tests/test_workflow_log_analysis_purge_safety.py (`_recent_doc()` at lines 49-51; `CASES` at line 46, which is the module loaded from tests/test_workflow_log_analysis_report_pr.py)
    - tests/test_workflow_log_analysis_report_pr.py:33 (`REPORT`, read only; do not change it)
    - tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py lines 4662 and 4669 (regexes `elapsed_ms=\d+`)
  steps:
    - In `_recent_doc()`, keep the "today minus two days" stamp in UTC. If the resulting path equals `CASES.REPORT`, use one day ago instead, so the returned path never equals `CASES.REPORT` and stays inside the retention window. Add a short comment that cites the 2026-11-11 collision.
    - In tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py, change `elapsed_ms=\d+` to `elapsed_ms=-?\d+` in the regexes at line 4662 (heartbeat) and line 4669 (failing-module END line), so they match line 4661. Keep the `rc=3` assertion as it is.
    - Do not change `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `tests/test_workflow_log_analysis_report_pr.py`, or anything related to the closed-reader / `gh_retry` test.
    - Run `tests/test_workflow_log_analysis_purge_safety.py` and the `test_full_body_overlaps_modules_and_fails_closed` test in `tests/test_ci_poll_test_sharding.py` to verify.

  equivalence_argument: Both edits remove dependence on the clock and the wall clock without weakening what the tests check. Purge-safety still seeds a recent doc that the purge must keep, and the timing test still checks the module, the line format and `rc=3`. Only the sign of the elapsed time is relaxed, the same way line 4661 already does.
  reversibility: Both are test-only edits on a few lines. If #9246 or #9271 lands an equivalent fix, the conflict resolves to either version, and a human can revert either edit without any effect on production.
